entities.summary:
Olaf II of Denmark (olaf-ii-of-denmark) was King of Denmark as Olaf II from 1376 and King of Norway as Olav IV from 1380 until his death on 1387-08-11. He was the son of Queen Margaret I of Denmark and King Haakon VI of Norway, and grandson of kings Magnus IV of Sweden and Valdemar IV of Denmark.



 Olaf II's reign was marked by the ongoing struggle for power between the Danish and Norwegian crowns, as well as the challenges posed by the Black Death, which ravaged Northern Europe during this period. He sought to strengthen his ties with the Hanseatic League, a powerful trading federation that dominated the Baltic region, and to promote the interests of the Danish-Norwegian monarchy.





 The legacy of Olaf II's reign can be seen in the continued rivalry between Denmark and Norway, as well as the lasting impact of the Black Death on European society. His efforts to strengthen the Danish-Norwegian monarchy also laid the groundwork for the unification of the two countries under a single ruler in the centuries to come.





 In the end, Olaf II's reign was cut short by his untimely death, but his impact on the history of the region was significant, and his memory continues to be felt to this day.
